mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete reconditioned Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 engine typically costs between £1,600 and £3,000 for supply only, while fully rebuilt units with upgraded components range from £2,500 to £4,000. Used engines are available from around £600.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of head gasket failure in a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Head gasket failure in the Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 usually presents as persistent overheating, unexplained coolant loss, and white smoke from the exhaust.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 valued between £5,000 and £10,000, a full rebuilt engine is a financially sound investment.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a Mk8 1.5 EcoBoost engine into a Mk7 Fiesta ST?

acceptedAnswer.text: While physically possible with extensive modification, fitting a Mk8 1.5L 3-cylinder EcoBoost engine into a Mk7 Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost is not a direct bolt-on swap.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply and fit for a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 engine typically takes 1 to 2 days once the engine has been delivered to the specialist workshop.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Mk7 Fiesta ST launched in 2013, it served as the high-performance hot hatch flagship of the Fiesta range, introducing the punchy 1.6L EcoBoost engine to replace the previous generation's naturally aspirated units. Over its production run, this engine became renowned for its tunability and engaging driving dynamics.

milestones.description: JTJA introduced, 1.6L EcoBoost, 182 PS (134 kW), featuring a twin-scroll turbocharger, overboost function, and mechanical limited-slip differential compatibility.
Minor facelift (Mk7.5), retaining the JTJA 1.6L EcoBoost engine but with updated infotainment and cosmetic tweaks.
Production of the 1.6L EcoBoost ST ended, replaced in the Mk8 generation by a 1.5L 3-cylinder EcoBoost producing 200 PS.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.question: What are the signs of head gasket failure in a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost?
items.answer: Head gasket failure in the Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Mk7 usually presents as persistent overheating, unexplained coolant loss, and white smoke from the exhaust.
keyPoints: You may notice a milky residue on the oil filler cap or dipstick.
The vehicle may enter limp mode to protect the engine from further thermal damage.
Ignoring these signs can lead to catastrophic piston or cylinder head damage.

items.question: Can I fit a Mk8 1.5 EcoBoost engine into a Mk7 Fiesta ST?
items.answer: While physically possible with extensive modification, fitting a Mk8 1.5L 3-cylinder EcoBoost engine into a Mk7 Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost is not a direct bolt-on swap.
keyPoints: It requires significant supporting modifications, including a custom ECU tune, different wiring harness, and adapted engine mounts.
The transmission and drivetrain components may also require adaptation to handle the different power delivery.
We recommend consulting a specialist performance tuner before attempting this conversion to ensure compatibility and reliability.
